Use Nx=400 uniform finite-volume cells on the domain x in [-1,1] with dx=2/400=0.005 and cell centers x_j=-1+(j+0.5)*dx for j=0,1,...,399.
Evolve conservative variables U=[rho, m, E] as cell averages with m=rho*v and E=p/(Gamma-1)+0.5*rho*v^2.
Use Gamma=1.6666666666666667, eta=0.1, zeta=eta=0.1, and CFL=0.4.
Use the equation of state p=(Gamma-1)*(E-0.5*m^2/rho) and clip rho and p to a floor of 1e-12 if needed.
Use the Rusanov numerical flux for the inviscid part with F_conv(U)=[m, m^2/rho+p, (E+p)*v] where v=m/rho.
Set the Rusanov wave speed at each interface as a=max(|v_L|+c_L, |v_R|+c_R) with c=sqrt(Gamma*p/rho).
Set the numerical convective flux as F_hat=0.5*(F_conv(U_L)+F_conv(U_R))-0.5*a*(U_R-U_L).
Compute v_x at cell centers with a centered difference using the cell-centered v values.
Compute sigma=(zeta+4/3*eta)*v_x at cell centers.
Approximate sigma at each interface by averaging the neighboring cell-centered sigma values.
Use interface-averaged v and sigma to form the viscous interface flux F_visc=[0, -sigma, -v*sigma].
Use the total interface flux F_total=F_hat+F_visc.
Integrate the semi-discrete system with 2-stage SSP-RK2 (Heun's method).
Choose the time step each step as dt_conv=CFL*dx/max_j(|v_j|+c_j), dt_visc=0.5*dx^2/max(zeta+4/3*eta, 1e-30), and dt=min(dt_conv, dt_visc).
Adjust the final time step so the final time T=0.5 is hit exactly.
Implement periodic boundary conditions by wrapping ghost-cell indices.
Set initial conditions at cell centers: rho(x,0)=1.0+0.2*sin(pi*x), v(x,0)=0.1*cos(pi*x), p(x,0)=1.0+0.2*cos(pi*x).
At final time T=0.5, compute rho(x,T), v(x,T), and p(x,T) on the cell centers.
Save the file solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz containing arrays x, rho, v, p and scalars Gamma, eta, zeta, T, dx, CFL.
Save the plot of rho, v, and p versus x at T as solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png.
Print the minimum and maximum of rho and p for the positivity check, and print the mean of rho over the domain for the mass conservation check.
When writing Python code, use ** for exponentiation.
